$comment: Manifest for the Punar topographic wallpaper plates.
Every plate is generated from USGS 3D Elevation Program (3DEP) 1/3 arc-second
elevation data, which is a work of the United States Government and is in the
public domain under 17 U.S.C. 105. No API key, account or attribution is
required; Punar credits USGS anyway in Wallpaper/SOURCES.md.
lat_span is the north-south extent in degrees. The longitude span is NOT
given here: tools/wallpaper_plate.py derives it as 1.6 * lat_span / cos(lat)
so every plate is exactly 16:10 ON THE GROUND. Writing both spans by hand is
how terrain silently ends up stretched, because a degree of longitude is
shorter than a degree of latitude everywhere but the equator.
interval_m is the contour spacing. It is per-place on purpose: a 3400 m
granite valley and an 800 m canyon do not read the same at one spacing.
interval_m is now the SUPPLEMENTARY (finest) spacing; intermediate is 2x and index is 5x.

label_lat/label_lon are a NAMED LANDMARK inside the frame, not the crop centre: the readout should say where you are looking, and 'Half Dome' is a truer answer than the arithmetic middle of a bounding box.
